To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fine tuning of ligand activity for VDR can be done by the 22-alky chain length of ligand.
the agonistic/antagonalistic activity for V DR can be controlled by 22- alkyl chain length of 22S-substituted 1α, 25-dihydroxyvitam in D3 analogs.
fine tuning of VDR agonistic/antagonal activity is possible by 2-alkyl chain of the ligands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the relationships between the 22-alkylation of ligands and agonistic/ antagonistic activity, and with the structural requirements for the design of VDR antagonists.
the alteration of pocket structures of VDR by the 22-alklyl substituent and the relationships between such alterations and agonistic/ antagonistic activity.

the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of action of VDR, which is one of the nuclear hormone receptors, and is expected to provide the basic information for the development of novel therapeutic agents for the treatment of vitamin D deficiency-related diseases such as osteoporosis and cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bulkier side chain is, in most cases, the stronger antagonistic activity is, but not always.
the 22-alky chain length of ligand is one of the most important factors for fine-tuning of agonistic/ antagonistic activity of ligand.
the agonistic activity is dominant when the VDR-lacking 22-alkyloxy chain is longer than C6, and the antagonistic activity is dominant for the VDR-possessing 22-alkoxy chain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 22S-H group of the ligand is the optimal structure for VDR agonist and the 22S-Et, Bu and Hex groups of the ligand are the optimal structures for VDR partial agonist and antagonists, respectively.
the 22-alkylation of ligands may be useful for the development of VDR agonists and antagonists.

the VDR-LDB is not necessarily in a conformation that can accommodate the 22-alkenyl chain of the natural agonist 1α, 25-dihydroxyvitamine D3 (1α, 2S-(OH)2D3) and the 22-acyl chain of the natural antagonist 22-oxacalcitriol (22-Oxo) in the same way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VDR-LBDB can be tuned to be agonistic or antagonistic, depending upon which ligand is bound to it, and this tuning can be controlled by altering the 22-alkylester side chains of the VDR ligands.
the 22S-H hexyl compound unexpectedly restored the agonistic activity.
22S-hydroxy group of 22S-alkyl compounds is important for the restoration of the agonistic activity.
